newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish quiet day lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish quiet day lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended a lackluster session lower, pressured by mild profit-taking after Friday's steep gains.
September Treasury bond futures rallied to an almost four-month high on Friday in the second heaviest volume T-bond futures session ever.
"I think today was just a little correction," a T-bond trader said. "Volume was nothing."
On Friday, T-bond futures traded 739,632 contracts, surpassing the former second-heaviest volume day of 737,065 set May 6, 1994.
Open interest Friday rose 27,417 contracts overall.

On Monday, September T-bonds dipped through support at 110-23/32 to 110-25/32 and hit a session low of 110-17/32 in late trading. Traders said flows overall were light, and September stayed confined to the upper part of Friday's range.
In addition to profit-taking, traders blamed Monday's losses on a weak dollar and an absence of economic news.
"It all came on light volume," said Don Pullen, trading floor bond manager with ED and F Man.
He said technical sales and the dollar started the tone, pushing September into a 110-20/32 to 110-14/32 support band.

Earlier in the session, prices showed scant reaction to news the U.S. Treasury was scrapping July and October conventional 10-year note sales and introducing a new five-year inflation-protected security.

"There were enough people that were talking about it on Friday that people were already discounting that," said Kurt Fraim, analyst with Aubrey Lanston. "I think that was part of the bid we had Friday."
Fraim agreed that action was light overall Monday, with only a few firms standing out as notable buyers.
Several traders noted that one major U.S. dealer was a reported seller of between 10,000 and 13,000 June T-bonds.

At the close, Sept T-bonds were down 20/32 at 110-19/32, 10-yr notes fell 11/32 to 108-6/32, munis fell 14/32 to 118-5/32, Sept bills were down 0.025 point at 94.670, Dec Euros fell 0.040 to 93.820. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
